    SteamOS Comes to More AYANEO Handhelds, Along With Native Frame Gen

    By andrewSeptember 27, 2026Updated:September 27, 2026No Comments4 Mins Read
    Facebook Twitter Copy Link LinkedIn Reddit WhatsApp Email
    AYANEO Pocket S2 and Pocket S2 Pro Promo Image 1
    Share
    Facebook Twitter Copy Link Reddit WhatsApp Email

    Instaread

    Lining up with the release of the Steam Frame, Valve made its ARM build of SteamOS available around the same time. Naturally, this prompted some in the community to jump on the train, offering SteamOS builds tweaked and tailored for a few of our favorite Android handhelds. One of which was simply named “SteamOS-ARM-SM8650,” which has already been updated twice over the past three days.

    The first update added a rather unique feature, in that it brought the Google Play Store into SteamOS. Not only that, but you’re able to download and install Android apps from the Play Store without ever needing to jump into Desktop Mode or tinker with Wayland.

    Another update for SteamOS-ARM-SM8650 was released earlier today, bringing with it a slight tweak to the name, with the project now being called “SteamOS ARM for Handhelds.” With v1.2, this build of SteamOS adds support for both the AYANEO Pocket S2 and Pocket S2 Pro, while also introducing a few ease-of-life features.

    The headlining feature of this release is ARM-native Lossless Scaling frame gen thanks to LSFG 2.0, which is accessible from within the pre-installed Decky plugin. Beyond that, the developer is aiming to make the installation and update process much easier, starting with an “Easy UFS Installer” app.

    This is available in Desktop Mode, and similar to Armada, lets you choose the amount of storage to dedicate to Android while partitioning the rest for SteamOS. As for future updates, there’s a new built-in SteamOS Update app, meaning that once you’ve installed v1.2, you shouldn’t find the need to re-flash the build in the future.

    If you want to check out the entire changelog, you’ll find it below. And if you’re ready to take the leap and throw this on your handheld, head over to the GitHub Releases page to get started.

    SteamOS ARM for handhelds

    Version
    1.3-beta2
    Description
    Official SteamOS ARM (Steam Frame build) for the KONKR Pocket FIT / Snapdragon 8 Gen 3 handhelds
    Key features
    • Game Mode, Desktop Mode, Steam store and downloads
    • x86 games through FEX, plus ARM64 Proton
    • Performance overlay
    • Lossless Scaling frame gen via deck-lsfg-vk plugin
    GitHub
    GitHub
    Download
    Download

    SteamOS ARM Handhelds v1.2 Changelog

    Native ARM frame gen + one-tap internal install

    Frame Gen, native on ARM

    • Lossless Scaling frame gen is on LSFG 2.0 now, with an ARM64 build for ARM64 games next to the plugin’s x86 one for games running through FEX.
    • The Decky plugin comes preinstalled and its Install button actually works now. You still need to own Lossless Scaling on Steam.
    • The ARM64 layer is lsfg-vk 2.0 by PancakeTAS, built from the official source with no code changes and shared under its CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 license.

    Install to internal storage

    • New Easy UFS Installer app in Desktop Mode. Pick how much space Android keeps and it does the rest. Android stays, and you pick which one to boot in the ABL menu.
    • It backs up your partition table to the SD card first, so you can always go back.

    No more reflashing

    • New SteamOS Update app. Future versions install over your current system and keep your games, saves, accounts and Wi-Fi. If an update gets cut off halfway, it rolls back on the next boot.
    • v1.1 doesn’t have the updater yet, so this is the last reflash.

    AYANEO Pocket S2 and S2 Pro

    • Initial support is in. Same chip and screen, so both run the same setup (on the Pro, pick AYANEO Pocket S2 as the device model in the ABL). I don’t have one, so if you do, please try it and tell me what works.

    Controls

    • Right stick no longer moves the triggers, and the menu buttons no longer act like a right-click.
    • The controller service was quietly using a whole CPU core in the background. Fixed, so a bit more battery and a bit less heat.

    Everything else

    • Newer gamescope, so the Steam UI runs at 144Hz and touch feels snappier.
    • Updated to the newest Steam Frame SteamOS base.
    • Play Store sign-in no longer gets blocked.
    • Switching to Desktop Mode takes about 3 seconds now, and Wi-Fi stays connected when you come back to Game Mode.
    • Fixed fan speed no longer jumps between your setting and 100%.
    • Speakers sound cleaner and don’t distort at max volume.
    • Desktop Mode has the Steam splash again, and Discover installs apps properly.
    • Hardware video decoding works.
    • SSH is off by default now. To turn it on, set a password with passwd in Konsole, then run sudo systemctl enable --now sshd.

    Armada’s Latest Update is Here with some Quality of Life Changes

    By BanSeptember 27, 2026No Comments3 Mins Read
    Facebook Twitter Copy Link LinkedIn Reddit WhatsApp Email
    Cyberpunk 2077 on AYN Odin 3 via Armada
    Share
    Facebook Twitter Copy Link Reddit WhatsApp Email

    Despite the recent appearance of the Steam Frame, and by extension SteamOS on Arm over the last week or so, the Armada team has continued their cooking. The team has already stated they don’t expect much change in the direction of Armada after that, and the recent update they’ve put out really shows that. With some nice quality of life upgrades and changes, Armada is continuing to evolve for the better.

    As always, I put out the recommendations to check out what the Armada team is cooking in their usual sources. And for them there’s the big three. Their website for all of the links you could ever need, their Github for the full rundown on this and past updates, and their Discord if you’d like to chat with their community a bit more.

    As always you’ll find their Changelog below for more information, with some of my personal favorites highlighted.

    • Improved sleep behavior
      • Lower power consumption on SM8550/SM8650/SM8750 during sleep. Up to 50% reduction in battery drain.
      • Faster Wi-Fi connection after waking from sleep.
    • New Armada Tools desktop app/command line interface
      • View device information, storage, IP addresses, and installed OS and Steam versions
      • Enable SSH, select Stable/Beta/Preview update channels, install OS updates, and roll back to the previous version without Steam running
      • Repair Steam by restoring the bundled client while preserving games, saves, accounts, and settings
    • Device and controller improvements
      • Increased Retroid Pocket 6 touchscreen sampling to 119hz from 28hz (@diogotr7)
      • Improved analog input and increased reporting to 250 Hz on RSInput controllers for Retroid Pocket 6 and AYN Odin 3 (@diogotr7)
      • Removed the built-in Odin 3 stick deadzone (@diogotr7)
      • Fixed DisplayPort detection on SM8250 Retroid devices (@Tom42-eu)
      • Fixed input freezes for devices connected through USB hubs/docks (@keks2293)
    • Graphics and game compatibility improvements:
      • Fixed Quick Access Menu appearing behind games
      • Fixed bottom screen Gamescope startup during display handoff
      • Added kernel support for FEX’s unaligned atomic emulation and backpatching
      • Added dependencies needed by EmuDeck
    • Waydroid improvements
      • Restored controller input, including handling hotplug and Android restarts without duplicate controllers appearing in Steam
      • Made Armada’s Android Mesa drivers available during first initialization
    • Armada Control improvements:
      • Added Simplified Chinese, Brazilian Portuguese, and European Portuguese translations (thanks @mydanyi and @Raxcoms)
      • Added conservative CPU governor support (thanks @dsancalm)
      • Updated default power profiles: Eco and Balanced use the conservative CPU governor
      • Removed the CPU realtime scheduling option because it caused stability problems
      • Fixed controller calibration and system commands when using native ARM64 Decky Loader
      • Added optional automatic sleep logs under Documents/sleep-logs, with detailed kernel tracing to help diagnose suspend and wake problems (thanks @xXJSONDeruloXx)
    • Armada Store improvements
      • Fixed startup failures caused by an unavailable Python module (@Janleyx)
      • Lossless Scaling plugin on version 0.12.8 (@Raxcoms)
    • Initial support for MANGMI Pocket Max and MANGMI Air Y Pro
      • Audio is Not Working at this Time
    • Added Armada OS ID
    • Added armada-rebase helper for switching image tags/testing forks
    • Consolidated packages into main repository
    • Updated Linux to 7.2.6, Mesa to 26.2.3, FEX to 2609, Gamescope to 3.16.29-ogc2, and NetworkManager to 1.58.1

    Of the updates stuff like initial support for Mangmi Devices is awesome to see and improvements towards battery drain will always be welcome. As Armada continues to improve, I can see a lot more people attempting to make the switch over to it for their devices. And that’ll be awesome to see in the near future. Until then, be sure to continue supporting the Armada team, and check out their Github for more information.
